title: Poppy, Jett, and the Stormy Ridge Rescue
markdown:
In Whisperwind, where peaks tickled the bellies of clouds, Poppy and Jett had their own ways of moving through the air. Poppy was a whisper of a girl who loved her falcons. Her favourite, Swiftwing, wore feathers like a sunrise. Jett was a blur of motion on Grit, his mountain bike — usually brown with adventure, today gleaming silver, ready to leap any rock he pointed at.

One afternoon the sky put on a show. A playful puff of wind grew into a low rumble, a giant yawning. Then a heavy swirling cloak of angry grey draped the valley. This storm wanted to rearrange things. A crack split the air. The mountain sighed. A huge chunk of Serpent’s Ridge — so sheer only the surest goats used it — crumbled away.

News ran faster than Jett could pedal downhill. Hikers who had been admiring the crisp air were trapped on a tiny ledge, cut off. Grown-ups in town creased. The usual climbing paths were buried under sharp rock and fallen earth.

“Too dangerous,” they whispered. “We might not reach them in time.”

The grey veil pressed down.

Poppy’s heart fluttered like a trapped moth. She watched the storm lash her cottage, wind at the panes. Swiftwing preened. A daring idea, sudden as lightning: he was faster than wind when he needed to be. He could carry a rescue line. But the ledge was too wobbly to land on.

The door burst. Jett tumbled in, hair a tangle, face smudged. “Poppy. They’re stuck. The ridge is a disaster.” His usual cheer was dim. He had already tried the main routes. Impassable.

Poppy’s eyes shone brighter than Swiftwing’s best feather. “Swiftwing can carry the line. He can’t land. We need someone who can handle paths most people wouldn’t dream of.” She looked at Jett.

His grin chased the gloom. “Me?” He knew a secret network of old goat tracks, barely a trail, winding under the shattered ridge. No adult would take Grit there in this weather. Jett and Grit thrived on daring. A flicker of an old tumble on a tricky path — then the hikers. The grin widened. “I can get right underneath them.”

So the plan was wind, wings, and wheels. Poppy tied a strong light rope to Swiftwing’s leg. “Fly true.” He launched, a sunrise flash against the dark.

Far below, Jett and Grit were already a blur. Icy rain pinged his helmet. The wind tried to tear them off like leaves. He dodged falling branches. Tires found grip on slick mud. He took narrow ledges that would flip a climber’s stomach. The roar was immense. Mud sprayed his face. His eyes stayed on the goal. Faint shouts of the climbers came on the wind.

Just as he reached a surprisingly stable patch directly beneath them, Swiftwing appeared. He circled once, dropped the line. It landed with a soft thud near Jett’s hand. For a moment the roar softened to the whirr of wings turning home.

Jett secured the line and pulled, a yell the wind swallowed. The climbers saw the rope. Fear melted into work. Inch by inch, they came down.

When the storm grew tired, the world smelled of damp earth and pine. Poppy and Jett met at the base. Swiftwing’s feathers glowed even in the washed-grey light. Grit was mud from rim to stem and looked triumphant. The hikers waved from below, faces etched with relief. No villain. No shining armour. Two friends, their own talents, a path nobody else would take.

Poppy touched Swiftwing’s wet shoulder. Jett wiped mud from Grit’s logo and left most of it. The ridge was broken. The line was not.
